memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You shall have no other gods before me.'" - Ex 20:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The first command is about exclusivity. Not "worship Me most" but "have no
others."

Israel had just left a land crowded with gods. Egypt had one for the river, one
for the sun, one for the harvest, one for the dead. You could add a god the way
you might add an insurance policy. God says: not with Me.

We assume this command is easy for us because we do not keep statues. But a god
is simply whatever we look to for security, identity, and meaning. Anything can
occupy that place. Money, career, a relationship, a child's success, our own
reputation, even ministry.

The test is not what we say we believe. It is what we turn to when we are
frightened, and what we cannot imagine living without.

Notice that this is the first command, and everything else follows from it. Get
this wrong and the rest unravels. Jesus was asked which commandment was greatest
and answered: love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, mind, and
strength (Mark 12:30). All. Not most.

This is not God being insecure. It is God being honest. He is the only one who
can actually bear the weight of our worship. Everything else will collapse under
it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What do you turn to first when you are afraid?
2. What could you not imagine your life without?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You alone are God. Show me what I have quietly placed beside You and help
me to let it go. Amen.
